info.name: Uyir authservice
info.description:
The Uyir `authservice` API (default http://localhost:4000).

Organised and documented to the platform **API Naming Convention** (`docs/API_NAMING_CONVENTION.md`). Where authservice deviates from the convention it is because of §12 ("authservice today — known deviations"):

- **No `/v1` prefix** yet — routes are `/api/v1/auth/email/login`, treated as v1 until the next breaking change.
- **Auth paths are grouped by flow, not resource** — `/api/v1/auth/email/*`, `/api/v1/auth/google/*`, `/api/v1/auth/token/refresh`. The "resource" is a session/token flow, not a CRUD entity.
- **Login / refresh responses are unwrapped** (`{ "accessToken": …, "role": … }`) for client compatibility. Newer endpoints (`/api/v1/auth/users/*`) wrap under the resource name (`{ "user": {…} }`, `{ "users": [...] }`).

Conventions that DO hold everywhere here:
- Error shape: `{ "error": { "code": "SCREAMING_SNAKE", "message": "…" } }`; validation errors add `details`. Clients branch on `code`, never on `message` or status alone.
- Request/response keys are `camelCase`; enum values (`role`, `status`) are `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE` strings.
- Identity is only ever `Authorization: Bearer <RS256 JWT>` — no `X-User-Id`, no user id in the URL for "me".
- `X-Request-Id` is propagated on every request (this collection sends one per request).

**Portals** (`clientId` in the request body / query — pick the one your caller represents):

| clientId | kind | roles | refresh token delivery | new account |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `patient-app` | native | PATIENT | body `refreshToken` | ACTIVE |
| `patient-portal` | web | PATIENT | httpOnly cookie | ACTIVE |
| `service-provider-app` | native, multi-role | DOCTOR / HOSPITAL / LS / AMBULANCE_DRIVER / PRO (send `role`) | body `refreshToken` | PENDING (needs admin approval) |
| `admin-portal` | web | ADMIN | httpOnly cookie | PENDING (needs SUPER_ADMIN approval) |
| `superadmin-portal` | web | SUPER_ADMIN | httpOnly cookie | ACTIVE |

Set `{{clientId}}` in the environment. Run **Email auth › Login** (or **Google auth › Native**) to populate `{{accessToken}}` / `{{refreshToken}}`.

item.name: Infrastructure
item.description: Unversioned infrastructure contracts (§2.4, §9). No auth, ever.

request.description: Liveness + a real dependency check (`SELECT 1`). `200 { "status": "ok" }` or `503 { "status": "unavailable" }`.
Public RS256 signing keys. Every other service fetches this once, caches by `kid`, refetches on a `kid` miss, and verifies access tokens locally (§10, §11).

item.name: Email auth
item.description: Email + password login flow. `/api/v1/auth/email/register`, `/api/v1/auth/email/login` and `/api/v1/auth/google/native` are rate limited (default 20 attempts / 15 min per IP → `429 RATE_LIMITED`).

exec: var body; try { body = pm.response.json(); } catch (e) { return; }
pm.test('role and status are SCREAMING_SNAKE enums', function () {

request.description:
Body: `email`, `password` (≥ 8 chars), `clientId` (portal). `role` is **only** used by multi-role portals (`service-provider-app`) and must be one of DOCTOR / HOSPITAL / LS / AMBULANCE_DRIVER / PRO — single-role portals ignore it, so drop the line for `patient-app`.

`201 { id, email, role, status, pendingApproval }`. `pendingApproval: true` (status `PENDING`) means an ADMIN / SUPER_ADMIN must approve before login works.

Errors: `VALIDATION_ERROR` (400), `UNKNOWN_PORTAL` (400), `ROLE_REQUIRED` / `ROLE_NOT_ALLOWED` (400), `CONFLICT_EMAIL_TAKEN` (409).

exec: var body; try { body = pm.response.json(); } catch (e) { return; }
// Native portals return the refresh token in the body; web portals set an httpOnly cookie.

request.description:
`200 { accessToken, role }` — plus `refreshToken` in the body for native portals; web portals instead get a `Set-Cookie` httpOnly refresh cookie.

Errors: `INVALID_CREDENTIALS` (401), `PENDING_APPROVAL` (403), `ACCOUNT_DISABLED` (403), `FORBIDDEN` (403, account role not served by this portal), `RATE_LIMITED` (429).

Start setting or resetting a password - one flow for a Google-first user who wants their first password AND for a genuine 'forgot password'. Always `202` regardless of whether the email has an account (no enumeration). On a real hit, authservice mints a 10-min single-use 6-digit code and emits a `PasswordResetRequested` event to Kafka; `notification-service` sends the email. Copy the code from that email into the environment as `{{resetOtp}}` for the next request.

Errors: `UNKNOWN_PORTAL` (400), `RATE_LIMITED` (429).

Redeem the emailed code and set the new password. Creates the PASSWORD login for a Google-first account, or replaces the hash for a genuine reset. On success every existing session on the account is revoked (all devices must re-login) and other outstanding codes are invalidated.

`204 No Content`. Errors: `INVALID_RESET_CODE` (400 - unknown email, or code wrong / used / expired), `RATE_LIMITED` (429).

exec: var body; try { body = pm.response.json(); } catch (e) { return; }

request.description:
Rotating refresh (§2.3 action endpoint). Native clients send `{ refreshToken }` in the body and get `{ accessToken, refreshToken }` back. Web clients send **no body** — the refresh cookie is read and a new one is set; response is `{ accessToken }`.

For a web portal, delete the body (send `{}`) and let Postman's cookie jar carry the cookie.

Errors: `NOT_AUTHENTICATED` (401, missing / unknown / expired / already-rotated token).
Revokes the one session behind the presented refresh token (body for native, cookie for web) and clears the cookie. `204` with no body — idempotent, `204` even if the token was already gone.

Acts on the whole account, so it needs a valid **access token** (`Authorization: Bearer`), not the refresh token. Revokes every session for the caller. `200 { revokedSessions: <n> }`.

Errors: `NOT_AUTHENTICATED` (401).

item.name: Google auth
item.description: Google sign-in. Web portals use the browser redirect flow (`/start` → Google → `/callback`); native portals POST a Google ID token to `/native`. Requires `GOOGLE_*` env config or every route here returns `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`.

query.description: Only for a multi-role WEB portal; omit otherwise.

request.description:
Sets a short-lived PKCE + state cookie and `302`-redirects to Google's consent screen. Turn OFF "Automatically follow redirects" in Postman settings to see the `Location` header.

Errors: `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` (503, Google not configured), `REDIRECT_URI_NOT_ALLOWED` (400), `UNKNOWN_PORTAL` (400), `PROVIDER_NOT_ALLOWED` (400), `USE_NATIVE_GOOGLE` (400, portal is a native client).

Google redirects the browser here. Exchanges the code, sets the refresh cookie, and `302`s back to the portal `redirectUri` with `?accessToken=…` (or `?error=<CODE>` on failure — e.g. `PENDING_APPROVAL`, `STATE_MISMATCH`, `ACCOUNT_DISABLED`). Normally driven by the browser, not called directly.

exec: var body; try { body = pm.response.json(); } catch (e) { return; }

request.description:
The app runs Google Sign-In with its own SDK, gets an ID token, and posts it here. No browser, no PKCE cookie. `role` required for `service-provider-app`. `200 { accessToken, role, refreshToken }`.

Errors: `VALIDATION_ERROR` (400), `NOT_A_NATIVE_CLIENT` (400), `PENDING_APPROVAL` (403), `RATE_LIMITED` (429).

item.name: Admin
item.description: Back-office user approval. Every route needs a valid **ADMIN** or **SUPER_ADMIN** access token (`403 FORBIDDEN` otherwise). Newer endpoints — responses wrap under the resource name (§6.1 / §6.2).

request.description: Users with `status: PENDING` that the caller may act on (an ADMIN sees provider accounts; a SUPER_ADMIN also sees pending ADMINs). `200 { users: [ … ] }`.

State-transition action (§2.3). Flips `PENDING → ACTIVE`. `200 { user: { … } }`.

Errors: `NOT_AUTHENTICATED` (401), `FORBIDDEN` (403), `NOT_FOUND` (404), `CONFLICT_NOT_PENDING` (409).
State-transition action (§2.3). Rejects a pending signup. `200 { user: { … } }`. Same error set as approve.

item.name: Convention reference (negative cases)
item.description: Requests that deliberately fail, to show the standard error envelope (§7) and status mapping (§8).

request.description: Missing `clientId`, invalid `email`, too-short `password`. `400 { error: { code: "VALIDATION_ERROR", message, details } }`.
